findings.issue_text: packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleSMSReminders.ts:190 — The retryCount update inside the catch block is itself unguarded, so if the row was deleted concurrently (booking cancel/reschedule, P2025) or the original failure was a DB error, it throws out of the for-loop and aborts scheduling of every remaining reminder in the batch, where previously the error was only logged.

packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleSMSReminders.ts:40 — With `retryCount > 1` only two failed cron ticks are allowed and transient vs permanent failures are counted the same, so a short Twilio/network outage hard-deletes every pending SMS reminder in the 7-day window with no log, alert, or user-visible signal, even though days remain before scheduledDate.

packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleSMSReminders.ts:38 — The new `retryCount > 1` OR branch in deleteMany has no `method: SMS` or `scheduled: false` filter, so this SMS cron hard-deletes any EMAIL/WHATSAPP (or already-scheduled) WorkflowReminder row whose table-wide retryCount goes above 1.

packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleSMSReminders.ts:169 — If twilio.scheduleSMS succeeds but the `scheduled/referenceId` update throws, the catch increments retryCount and leaves scheduled=false, so the next tick schedules a duplicate SMS, and once retries run out the row is deleted, leaving Twilio messages with no stored referenceId to cancel.

packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleSMSReminders.ts:184 — Both increments write the stale read value `reminder.retryCount + 1` instead of an atomic `{ increment: 1 }`, so overlapping cron invocations lose increments and undercount retries.

packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleSMSReminders.ts:158 — Permanent failures where no message or sendTo resolves (and the `continue` at line 68 for a missing step/booking) never increment retryCount, so retry tracking skips them and they are silently re-processed on every tick.

packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleSMSReminders.ts:38 — The new `retryCount > 1` OR branch has no `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` filter, so the SMS cron will delete EMAIL/WHATSAPP reminders once anything else uses retryCount.

adjudication.rationale: In scheduleSMSReminders.ts the catch block now performs an awaited prisma.workflowReminder.update(...) (incrementing retryCount) before logging. That update is not wrapped in its own try/catch, so if it throws (e.g., record deleted concurrently causing Prisma P2025, or the original failure was a DB connectivity/error that persists), the exception will escape the catch and abort the remaining iterations of the reminder loop. Previously the catch only logged the error, so failures would not stop scheduling the rest of the batch.

Since `retryCount` is incremented on scheduling failure (both the `else` branch and `catch`), a transient Twilio/network outage over ~2 cron runs can cause future (still-in-window) reminders to be hard-deleted with no logging or user-visible signal. This is concrete data loss behavior introduced by the diff.

On the next run, the reminder can be re-scheduled (duplicate SMS). Additionally, the new cleanup deletes reminders with `retryCount > 1`, so repeated update failures can delete the row while Twilio messages exist without a stored `referenceId`.

That update can itself throw (e.g., record deleted concurrently or DB error), in which case the exception will propagate out of the loop/handler and prevent processing remaining reminders, and the original `console.log` line will never run because it comes after the update.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleSMSReminders.ts:40 — gt: 1` permanently deletes a reminder after only 2 failed attempts (about two cron runs), even when its scheduledDate is days away, so a short Twilio outage now drops reminders that the old code would have retried.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes the initial cleanup `deleteMany` to `OR: [{ method: SMS, scheduledDate <= now }, { retryCount: { gt: 1 } }]`. Since `retryCount` is incremented on scheduling failure (both the `else` branch when no `sid` and in the `catch`), any reminder that reaches `retryCount = 2` will be deleted on the next cron run regardless of `scheduledDate` (and regardless of `method`, since the retryCount clause is not scoped). This matches the finding: reminders can be dropped after ~2 failed attempts even if their scheduledDate is still days away.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleSMSReminders.ts:190 — The catch also runs when twilio.scheduleSMS succeeded but the `scheduled: true`/referenceId update threw, so a live Twilio-scheduled SMS gets retried or deleted without its referenceId and can no longer be cancelled.

adjudication.rationale: The try/catch appears to wrap both the Twilio scheduling call and the subsequent Prisma update that sets `scheduled: true` and `referenceId` (seen at the `await prisma.workflowReminder.update({ data: { scheduled: true, referenceId: scheduledSMS.sid } })` block). If Twilio scheduling succeeds but that Prisma update throws, control goes to the `catch`, which now increments `retryCount` (`retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1`) without persisting the Twilio `sid`. This leaves a live Twilio-scheduled SMS with no stored `referenceId` and the reminder may be retried (duplicating sends) and/or later deleted by the new cleanup `deleteMany` condition `OR: [{...past scheduledDate...}, { retryCount: { gt: 1 } }]`, making cancellation/improper tracking impossible.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleSMSReminders.ts:184 — The retry count is written as a read-modify-write (`reminder.retryCount + 1`) from a stale findMany snapshot instead of an atomic `{ increment: 1 }`, so overlapping cron runs can lose increments.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `retryCount` and updates it via `data: { retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1 }` (both in the `else` branch after checking `scheduledSMS.sid` and in the `catch`). Since `reminder.retryCount` comes from a prior `findMany` snapshot, concurrent/overlapping runs can read the same old value and write back the same incremented value, losing increments. Prisma supports atomic updates (e.g., `{ retryCount: { increment: 1 } }`), which would avoid this race; the current code is a real correctness issue under concurrency.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleSMSReminders.ts:38 — The `retryCount > 1` OR-arm of deleteMany is not scoped to `method: SMS`, so this SMS cron hard-deletes any EMAIL/WHATSAPP WorkflowReminder rows whose table-wide retryCount column exceeds 1.

adjudication.rationale: In scheduleSMSReminders.ts the deleteMany filter was changed to `where: { OR: [ { method: SMS, scheduledDate <= now }, { retryCount: { gt: 1 } } ] }`. The second OR arm has no `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` constraint, so this SMS scheduling cron will delete any WorkflowReminder row (including EMAIL/WHATSAPP/etc.) whose new table-wide `retryCount` exceeds 1. That is unintended cross-method data deletion introduced by this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/prisma/schema.prisma:1000 — New `retryCount` column has no index, and the unindexed OR arm in the cron deleteMany forces a full sequential scan of the whole (large, all-methods) WorkflowReminder table every run instead of using the existing (method, scheduled, scheduledDate) index.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `retryCount` (default 0) without adding any `@@index([retryCount])`, and updates the cron cleanup query to `deleteMany({ where: { OR: [{ method: SMS, scheduledDate <= now }, { retryCount: { gt: 1 } }] } })`. That new OR arm can plausibly make the delete query less index-friendly and may cause broader scans on `WorkflowReminder` depending on DB/query planner, so it’s a concrete performance concern introduced by the change. However, the finding’s claim about an existing `(method, scheduled, scheduledDate)` index is not verifiable from the shown schema snippet (we only see indexes on `bookingUid` and `workflowStepId` here).

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleSMSReminders.ts:184 — retryCount is written as a read-modify-write (`reminder.retryCount + 1`) instead of an atomic `{ increment: 1 }`, so overlapping cron runs can lose increments and undercount retries.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `retryCount` and updates it via `data: { retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1 }` (in both the `else` branch and the `catch`). This is a read-modify-write based on a previously read value from `findMany`, so concurrent/overlapping executions can race and overwrite each other, losing increments. Prisma supports atomic updates (e.g., `{ retryCount: { increment: 1 } }`), which would avoid this correctness issue.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleSMSReminders.ts:38 — The new unscoped `OR { retryCount: { gt: 1 } }` branch filters on an unindexed column with no `method` predicate, so the per-cron-tick deleteMany can no longer use the `[method, scheduled, scheduledDate]` index and falls back to a full sequential scan of the whole WorkflowReminder table (all methods).

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show an unscoped `OR` branch `{ retryCount: { gt: 1 } }` in `deleteMany`, and `retryCount` is added without any explicit index in the shown Prisma model snippet. However, the finding’s central claim that this change prevents use of a specific existing `[method, scheduled, scheduledDate]` index cannot be verified from the diff: the schema excerpt only shows `@@index([bookingUid])` and `@@index([workflowStepId])`, and nothing in the diff confirms the referenced compound index or the guaranteed fallback to a full sequential scan.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleSMSReminders.ts:190 — The un-guarded prisma update inside the catch block can itself throw (e.g. P2025 if the reminder was deleted by a concurrent booking cancel, or DB blip), aborting the whole cron loop so remaining reminders are skipped, the handler 500s, and the original error is never logged since console.log runs after the update.

adjudication.rationale: In the new catch block (and also the new `else` branch), the code performs `await prisma.workflowReminder.update({ where: { id: reminder.id }, data: { retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1 } })` without guarding it. Prisma `update` can throw (e.g., record no longer exists -> P2025, transient DB error). Because `console.log` comes after the update in the catch, a thrown update would skip logging and escape the per-reminder try/catch, potentially aborting the loop and causing the handler to error. This behavior is directly implied by the added code in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleSMSReminders.ts:40 — Retry budget of `retryCount > 1` (two failed cron ticks) with transient and permanent failures counted identically means a brief Twilio/network outage permanently deletes every pending SMS reminder in the 7-day window despite days of remaining slack before scheduledDate.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a cleanup `deleteMany` with `where: { OR: [ { method: SMS, scheduledDate <= now }, { retryCount: { gt: 1 } } ] }`. Because the `retryCount > 1` branch is not constrained by `method` or `scheduledDate`, any reminder (including future scheduled SMS within the 7-day window) will be permanently deleted once its `retryCount` exceeds 1. The same diff increments `retryCount` on scheduling failure (`else` branch when `scheduledSMS` is falsy) and in the `catch`, so a transient Twilio/network outage across two cron runs would cause reminders to hit `retryCount=2` and then be deleted on the next run despite still having time before `scheduledDate`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleSMSReminders.ts:38 — The `retryCount > 1` OR-branch of deleteMany has no `method: SMS` (or `scheduled: false`) filter, so it silently deletes EMAIL/WHATSAPP (and already-scheduled) WorkflowReminder rows with retryCount > 1, and exhausted reminders are dropped with no log or alert.

adjudication.rationale: In scheduleSMSReminders.ts, the deleteMany `where` was changed to `OR: [...]` where the second branch is only `{ retryCount: { gt: 1 } }` with no `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` (or other narrowing like `scheduled: false`). As written, this will delete *any* WorkflowReminder row (including EMAIL/WHATSAPP and already-scheduled ones) that has `retryCount > 1`, which is unintended data loss in an SMS-specific scheduling endpoint, and it happens silently (no log/alert in this code path).

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleSMSReminders.ts:169 — If twilio.scheduleSMS succeeds but the `scheduled/referenceId` update throws, the catch increments retryCount leaving scheduled=false, so the next tick schedules a duplicate SMS and after exhaustion the row is deleted, orphaning the Twilio-scheduled message with no referenceId to cancel it.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `retryCount` increments in both the `else` branch and the `catch` without marking the reminder as scheduled, and also adds deletion of any `WorkflowReminder` with `retryCount > 1` (`deleteMany` OR clause). If `twilio.scheduleSMS(...)` succeeds but the subsequent `prisma.workflowReminder.update({... scheduled: true, referenceId: scheduledSMS.sid })` throws, the `catch` will run and only increment `retryCount`, leaving the row still considered unscheduled for the next run (so it can schedule again, duplicating the SMS). After enough failures, the new cleanup (`retryCount > 1`) can delete the row, losing the ability to correlate/cancel the already-scheduled Twilio message because no `referenceId` was persisted.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleSMSReminders.ts:184 — Increment uses the stale read value `reminder.retryCount + 1` instead of an atomic `{ increment: 1 }`, so overlapping cron invocations can lose increments.

adjudication.rationale: The diff increments `retryCount` via a read-modify-write (`retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1`) in two `prisma.workflowReminder.update` calls. If two handler executions update the same reminder concurrently, one update can overwrite the other’s increment (lost update). Using an atomic Prisma update like `{ retryCount: { increment: 1 } }` would avoid this race.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleSMSReminders.ts:158 — Permanent failures where no message or sendTo is resolved (and the `continue` at line 68 for missing step/booking) never increment retryCount, so the retry tracking does not cover them and they are re-processed every tick until scheduledDate passes.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows retryCount being selected and incremented only in two places: when scheduling returns a falsy value (the new `else` after creating the scheduled reminder) and in the `catch` block. The finding claims there are additional early `continue` paths (e.g., missing step/booking at “line 68”, or no message/sendTo resolved) that bypass these increments, but those control-flow branches are not present in the provided diff hunks, so this behavior cannot be verified from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleSMSReminders.ts:29 — New retry-tracking behavior (retryCount increment on failure plus threshold deletion) ships with no tests; the diff touches no test files and nothing in the repo exercises this cron handler.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds nontrivial retry logic in `scheduleSMSReminders.ts` (selecting `retryCount`, incrementing it on failure in both the `else` branch and `catch`, and deleting reminders where `retryCount > 1` via the new `OR` clause) plus a schema/migration adding `retryCount`. The PR diff touches no test files and contains no added coverage for this new behavior, so the concern about shipping new retry/deletion behavior without tests is grounded in what’s shown.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleSMSReminders.ts:38 — The retryCount OR branch has no `method: SMS` filter, and no test checks that EMAIL/WHATSAPP reminders with retryCount>1 survive the deleteMany (an integration test seeding non-SMS rows would catch this).

adjudication.rationale: In `scheduleSMSReminders.ts`, the `deleteMany` filter was changed to an `OR` where the second branch is `{ retryCount: { gt: 1 } }` without `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS`. This means *any* `WorkflowReminder` row (including EMAIL/WHATSAPP/etc.) with `retryCount > 1` will be deleted by this SMS-specific handler, which is a correctness/data-loss risk introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleSMSReminders.ts:40 — No test pins the `gt: 1` threshold boundary: retryCount=1 should be kept and retried, retryCount=2 should be deleted on the next run, so an off-by-one against the intended max-retries goes unnoticed.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces new retry deletion logic in `deleteMany` using `retryCount: { gt: 1 }` (i.e., delete when retryCount >= 2) and increments `retryCount` on failures. The PR diff shows no accompanying tests to lock down this off-by-one boundary behavior (retryCount=1 kept vs retryCount=2 deleted), so an intended max-retry policy could drift unnoticed. This is a specific, change-driven test gap rather than a verifiable defect in the code itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleSMSReminders.ts:178 — There is no test for the path where twilio.scheduleSMS returns a falsy value; it should assert retryCount goes up by exactly 1 and that scheduled/referenceId stay unchanged.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds new nontrivial behavior when `twilio.scheduleSMS(...)` returns a falsy value: an explicit `else` branch increments `retryCount` (`retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1`) without updating `scheduledDate`/`referenceId`. No corresponding test changes are shown in this PR diff to cover/verify that new branch and its persistence behavior, so calling out a missing test for this path is a specific, diff-grounded review concern rather than a functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleSMSReminders.ts:190 — There is no test for the catch-block update itself rejecting (e.g. row deleted or DB error); that would abort the whole loop and fail the cron for the remaining reminders, and a test should assert later reminders still get processed.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds new error-handling logic that updates `retryCount` both in the `else` branch and inside `catch` (both call `prisma.workflowReminder.update(...)`). If that `update` itself throws (e.g., row deleted, DB error), there is no surrounding try/catch for that secondary failure, so the handler could throw and stop processing subsequent reminders. The finding’s point is specifically about lacking a test for this new edge case; the diff shows no test additions and the new failure mode is introduced by the added `update` calls in the error paths.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleSMSReminders.ts:189 — No test covers a throw from the success-path update at line 169 after Twilio already scheduled the SMS; the catch still increments retryCount, so a real-DB test should pin whether that reminder is retried (duplicate SMS) or deleted.

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, the Twilio scheduling and the DB update that records success occur in the same `try`. If Twilio successfully schedules the SMS but the subsequent Prisma `update` (the “success-path update”) throws, execution goes to `catch`, which unconditionally increments `retryCount` (`retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1`). That can cause the reminder to be retried even though an SMS may already have been scheduled, potentially creating duplicates before `deleteMany` later removes records with `retryCount > 1`. The finding’s core point (this edge case isn’t pinned by tests and the retry behavior is ambiguous/important) is grounded in the shown control flow; the claim about “no test covers” can’t be verified from the diff, but the underlying scenario is real and worth addressing.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleSMSReminders.ts:184 — A mock-only test asserting `data: { retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1 }` would just echo the implementation; the multi-run lifecycle (fail, fail, deleted; or fail then succeed) needs a stateful test (prismock/real DB) over repeated handler calls.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds new stateful retry behavior: `retryCount` is persisted (schema/migration), incremented on failure paths (`update` with `retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1` in both the `else` branch and `catch`), and old reminders are deleted when `retryCount > 1` via `deleteMany` with an `OR` clause. Verifying this correctly requires tests that observe DB state across multiple handler runs (fail->increment->eventual delete or succeed), and a pure mock assertion of the update payload would largely mirror the implementation without validating the lifecycle. This is a concrete, diff-specific testing gap, not a direct defect in the shown code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleSMSReminders.ts:158 — No test pins the behavior when the message is empty or sendTo is missing: retryCount is never incremented, so these reminders sit outside the retry mechanism until scheduledDate passes.
